lead: Port St. Lucie plumbing deals with hurricanes, sandy soil and block homes from the 1980s on. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Port St. Lucie.
risk: slab leaks, polybutylene pipe and hurricane damage
risk_short: slab leaks, old pipes and storms
why: Port St. Lucie grew fast from the 1980s on, with mostly concrete block homes on slabs. Homes from the 1980s and early 1990s may have gray polybutylene pipe.
Hurricanes bring flooding and long power outages. Many older homes were built on septic systems, and the city has been connecting some areas to sewer.
water: Port St. Lucie treats water from the Floridan Aquifer using reverse osmosis. The water is soft after treatment.
tips: Look for gray pipe stamped PB2110.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
Know whether your home is on septic or sewer.
areas: PipeMend works in St. Lucie West, Tradition, Torino, Sandpiper Bay, Southbend, Floresta and every other Port St. Lucie neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Port St. Lucie Building Department, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faq.q: Do many Port St. Lucie homes have polybutylene pipe?
faq.a: Some homes from the 1980s and early 1990s do. Look for gray plastic pipe stamped PB2110. Many insurers ask about it, and replacing it avoids sudden leaks.
